column1: Concept: Classification
column2: Definition: A predictive task that learns a model to map input attributes to a categorical class attribute. Example: Classifying credit card transactions as either legitimate or fraudulent.

column1: What type of target attribute does classification aim to predict?
column2: A discrete or categorical class attribute.

column1: What is the primary goal of the classification task in data mining?
column2: To construct a model that accurately predicts the class label of unlabeled data based on its input attributes.

column1: How is a classification model learned using historical data?
column2: By analyzing a training set composed of records with known attribute values and pre-assigned class labels.

column1: What are two examples of classification applied in cybersecurity and medical diagnosis?
column2: Identifying network intruders in cyberspace and predicting whether tumor cells are benign or malignant.

column1: In a credit card fraud detection classification model, what constitutes the class attribute?
column2: The binary label indicating whether a historical transaction was fraudulent or fair.

column1: How does customer churn prediction utilize classification modeling?
column2: It uses demographic and behavioral customer attributes to predict the categorical decision label of whether a customer will buy or not buy a product.

column1: Concept: Regression
column2: Definition: A predictive task that estimates the value of a continuous variable based on other variables using a linear or nonlinear dependency model. Example: Predicting sales amounts of a new product based on advertising expenditure.

column1: How does regression differ from classification with respect to the target variable?
column2: Regression predicts a continuous-valued variable, whereas classification predicts a categorical class attribute.

column1: What is an environmental science example of a regression task?
column2: Predicting wind velocities as a function of continuous atmospheric variables like temperature, humidity, and air pressure.

column1: What is a financial application of regression modeling?
column2: Time series prediction of stock market indices.

column1: Concept: Clustering
column2: Definition: A descriptive task that groups data objects such that objects within the same group are similar and objects in different groups are distinct. Example: Subdividing retail customers into market segments based on demographic and lifestyle data.

column1: In cluster analysis, intra-cluster distances are _____ while inter-cluster distances are _____.
column2: minimized; maximized

column1: Is cluster analysis categorized as a predictive or descriptive data mining method?
column2: Descriptive

column1: How is document clustering applied in web news services like Google News?
column2: By grouping articles that share frequent key terms and high content similarity into distinct news topics.

column1: What scientific application uses K-means clustering to analyze earth observation data?
column2: Partitioning Sea Surface Temperature (SST) and Net Primary Production (NPP) datasets into clusters reflecting the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

column1: Concept: Association Rule Discovery
column2: Definition: A descriptive task that extracts dependency rules to predict the occurrence of an item based on the occurrences of other items in a transaction dataset. Example: Discovering that retail customers who buy diapers and milk are also likely to buy beer.

column1: In market-basket analysis, what does an association rule like $\{\text{Milk}\} \rightarrow \{\text{Coke}\}$ indicate?
column2: That transactions containing milk have a strong statistical likelihood of also containing Coke.

column1: How can retailer management use an association rule where Bagels are in the antecedent and Potato Chips are in the consequent?
column2: They can design joint sales promotions or optimize shelf placement to boost the sales of Potato Chips.

column1: How is association rule discovery applied in medical informatics?
column2: It discovers frequent combinations of patient symptoms and diagnostic test results that are associated with specific diseases.

column1: Data mining tasks are broadly categorized into _____ methods and _____ methods.
column2: predictive; descriptive

column1: What distinguishes predictive data mining tasks from descriptive data mining tasks?
column2: Predictive methods use variables to forecast unknown values, whereas descriptive methods find human-interpretable patterns that summarize the data.
